besluite.fout: 'eienskappe wys op iets wat ons daarvan maak' is vague and wooden; properties do not 'point to' an object
besluite.rede: 'pas by' says plainly that a property suits a use, keeps 'baie' and adds no fact.

besluite.fout: missing AWS comma between two clauses with their own subject and verb; the run of 'en ... en' makes a reader stumble
besluite.rede: Both halves are full clauses, so the AWS comma is required and also separates the list 'hard en sterk' from the clause join.

besluite.fout: missing AWS comma between two full clauses
besluite.rede: 'Die metaal is nie ... nie' and 'die verskil sit ...' each have their own subject and verb.

besluite.fout: a hand cannot name something; 'voel daardie hitte weggaan' is a stiff construction
besluite.rede: 'voel hoe ... weggaan' is the natural construction and 'jy noem dit koud' gives 'noem' a proper subject; the heat flow, its direction and 'hitte' are unchanged.

besluite.fout: missing AWS comma between two full clauses
besluite.rede: 'Koue kom nie ... nie' and 'net hitte beweeg' each have their own subject and verb.

besluite.fout: 'party' with an uncountable material reads awkwardly
besluite.rede: 'party soorte vlekvrye staal' is natural and states the same claim, since it is the kind of stainless steel that decides whether a magnet attracts it.

besluite.fout: three stacked 'en's in one sentence read clumsily
besluite.rede: One list says exactly the same four metals are not attracted, more clearly and in fewer words.

besluite.fout: comma before 'en' where the second part is elliptical and has no subject and verb of its own
besluite.rede: Under the AWS rule the house follows, no comma goes before 'en' between parts of one sentence; the meaning is unchanged.

besluite.fout: missing AWS comma between two main clauses; without it 'die reën en 'n rooibruin laag' can be misread as one phrase
besluite.rede: The imperative clause and 'n rooibruin laag vorm' are two full clauses, and the comma prevents a stumble.

besluite.fout: missing AWS comma between two full clauses
besluite.rede: 'Droë yster ... roes nie' and 'yster onder water ... roes ook nie' each have their own subject and verb.

besluite.fout: missing AWS comma between two full clauses
besluite.rede: 'Staal word ... gemaak' and 'n staalhek roes' each have their own subject and verb.

besluite.fout: missing AWS comma between two full clauses
besluite.rede: 'Roes skilfer af' and 'dan roes die yster daaronder ook' each have their own subject and verb.

besluite.fout: missing AWS comma between two full clauses
besluite.rede: 'Verf lê bo-op' and 'n krap laat ... roes' each have their own subject and verb.

besluite.fout: 'met tyd' is a calque of 'with time'; Afrikaans says 'mettertyd'
besluite.rede: 'mettertyd' fixes the calque, and 'deur' still names the gases as the cause of the darkening, so who does what is unchanged.
'slyt' is current standard Afrikaans alongside 'verslyt', so this is a lateral swap.

besluite.fout: missing AWS comma between two clauses with their own subject and verb
besluite.rede: 'goud bly blink' and 'silwer word net dof' are two full clauses.

besluite.fout: 'groot gewig dra' leans towards the figurative idiom 'to carry great weight' (to be important)
besluite.rede: 'swaar gewig' is the natural literal collocation and keeps the meaning that steel bears heavy loads.
This rewords a glossary definition, and 'wanneer lug en water bykom' is already idiomatic Afrikaans for air and water reaching the iron.

besluite.fout: 'met tyd' is a calque of 'with time'; Afrikaans says 'mettertyd'
besluite.rede: The fault is real, but it sits in the glossary definition of 'vlek', which may be shared word for word across lessons and changes only through the writer.
